_what: D5 hash-lock of THE CORPUS. The fifth lock's first half; derived_schema_hash is the second.
_why: The claim is that the suite every number is measured against existed, complete and unchangeable, BEFORE the first patch was written. That claim is about a moment, so the record names the commit and its timestamp rather than only the hash.
_hash_covers: sha256 over the JCS canonical bytes of each covered file, assembled with its repo-relative path into one payload and hashed again. Covered: corpus/training/*.json, fixtures/benign/*.json, corpus/pairs.json, corpus/F4-MANIFEST.json, and the `fingerprint` field of docs/proof/sealed-family-commitment.json. The coverage decision and its citations live in corpus/freeze.py.
_hash_does_not_cover: The nine known-bad calibration fixtures (their digests are below, outside the hash - KB5 carries a rate and KB6/KB8 an explicit null, and canonicalization restrictions 4 and 5 forbid both in a hashed payload; editing a calibration fixture so a hash will accept it is weakening a gate to fit a check). Also out: capability manifest Part A (manifest_hash, D3), derived_schema.json (derived_schema_hash, D5), and every .py and .md under corpus/.
canonicalization: RFC 8785 (JCS) plus the seven CRUCIBLE restrictions, canonicalization.md. NOT the textual contract-file normalization.

references._why: execution-spec D5 item 3: the corpus is hashed and committed 'referencing the frozen target hash and the gate rule hash'. These are REFERENCED, not hashed into the payload - a corpus_hash that moved when the target was re-frozen would stop being a function of the corpus. The reference is load-bearing because this script REFUSES when either prior record is absent.

sealed_family._how: BY REFERENCE ONLY. corpus/sealed/ is gitignored and its content is never read here - a read across that boundary is RUN INVALID. Two already-published content-addressed digests carry it into the hash instead: the 24 instance_ids and set_digest inside corpus/F4-MANIFEST.json, and the fingerprint in docs/proof/sealed-family-commitment.json.
sealed_family._consequence: corpus_hash is IDENTICAL on a machine holding the sealed set and on a fresh public clone that does not. Adding the sealed files changes nothing, because there is nothing to add. That is what makes this hash reproducible by a judge.

sealed_not_covered_by_commit_check: corpus/sealed/ is gitignored and can never be committed, so the uncommitted-changes refusal structurally CANNOT cover it. What IS asserted is different and is stated rather than assumed: scripts/seal-commitment.py --verify reported SEAL INTACT on this machine, meaning the sealed bytes still match the published fingerprint that is inside corpus_hash.

known_bad_calibration._why_recorded_anyway: known_bad_count: 9 is a frozen C7 parameter and G1(a) asserts each fixture's expected verdict every round, but neither covers a known-bad's CONTENT. A KB whose body moved without flipping its verdict would touch no hash-lock. These digests close that gap with evidence rather than with a hash the payload cannot legally carry.
known_bad_calibration._algorithm: sha256 over LF-normalized file bytes (canonicalization.md section 4, the textual form).

why_the_repairing_lane_could_not_fire_it: scripts/freeze-d5-corpus.py refuses on uncommitted changes, and the lane was not permitted to commit.
It refuses when corpus/sealed/ is absent from the checkout, which it is here. Ruling 52 already established that this freeze fires from the seal worktree.

python -m corpus therefore exits 1 on E_SEALED_BELOW_FLOOR - the sealed set holds 0 against an absolute floor of 18 - which is a third refusal and is pre-existing in this checkout, not caused by the repair.

It refuses over a record naming a different hash. THAT refusal is the one this archive answers: the guard demands a coordinator ruling with a written statement of what the move invalidates, and ruling 55 plus this block are it.
what_the_coordinator_must_run: 3. From the seal worktree, where corpus/sealed/ is present: confirm python -m corpus exits 0, remove the now-stale live record docs/proof/d5-corpus-freeze.json (this archive is the preserved copy - a superseded record is never deleted), and run python scripts/freeze-d5-corpus.py --write.
4. Read the new value off the record it writes. Do not copy it anywhere.
5. Re-take the derived-schema half in the same session - see the_derived_schema_half below.
6. Re-run python -m pytest -q and expect exit 0.

what_it_invalidates.the_60_bundles_of_2026_08_25: evidence/batch-night-2026-08-25/ - 60 bundles, 1,770 episodes, 95 promotions - was measured against a corpus THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. Each bundle carries the pre-repair corpus_hash in its own lock block, which is correct and stays correct: a bundle says what it said. What it may no longer do is be pooled, compared or averaged with any run taken after the re-freeze. Two suites, two denominators.
what_it_invalidates.no_rate_from_that_batch_was_quotable_ANY: Ruling 55's guard is explicit: if any instance is flagged DEGENERATE the run is INVALID and no rate is quoted from it. scripts/no-events-census.py flags exactly one instance DEGENERATE over that batch and it is this one, at 59 of 60 episodes with no tool call. So the repair takes away no number anybody was entitled to. It is what makes the NEXT batch quotable.
what_it_invalidates.the_95_promotions: They happened and remain facts about that run. What is invalidated is any effectiveness, transfer or convergence figure computed from them, because the attack suite those rules were fitted to and scored against is retired. The rules are artifacts, not measurements.
what_it_invalidates.the_instance_id_moves: instance_id is content-addressed over the whole instance body, so adding a turn moves it. The pre-repair id atk_3336f8347516 no longer resolves against the corpus. Every appearance of it - in evidence/, in docs/design/e-no-events-conflation-2026-08-25.md, in docs/design/e-no-events-split-design-2026-08-25.md, in docs/decisions-pending/live-corpus-and-worlds-2026-08-23.md and in tests/test_no_events_census.py - is a reference to the PRE-REPAIR instance and is correct as history. None is rewritten: a record says what it said.
what_it_invalidates.the_D5_blindness_result: Must be RE-MEASURED at freeze time over all 100 instances including the sealed set, not carried. Same consequence ruling 52 stated for the same reason: it is a claim about this corpus and the corpus moved. The label-blindness run performed during this repair saw 76 instances, because the sealed set is off-tree in this checkout, so it does not discharge the requirement.
what_it_invalidates.the_derived_schema_half: derived_schema_hash does NOT move, and its own record says why: the hash excludes blindness_check.max_predictive_accuracy as a rate, so 'this hash does not depend on the corpus'. But the blindness_check BLOCK recorded beside it was measured over 100 instances, one of which changed. Ruling 52 required the derived-schema record to be re-taken with the corpus so both halves of the fifth lock describe the same bytes. Re-take it in the same seal-worktree session.

what_it_does_NOT_invalidate.no_published_figure: Because there are none. Every figure in the repository's Results table is a design target from docs/measurement-spec.md section 8.1.

what_it_does_NOT_invalidate.the_attack_itself: The FINAL turn - the string RED_STRATEGIST rewrites, and the only one CorpusAttack.instruction carries - is UNCHANGED, character for character. It does not soften the ask, and it does not turn an attack into a benign request.

_superseded.what_the_repair_could_not_prove: That the repaired instance now produces a tool call. Proving it needs a live campaign and model spend, which the repairing lane was not permitted to run. The claim made here is narrower and is checkable offline: the instruction now names an order the episode's own world holds, so the target CAN act, where before it could not. Whether it DOES is the next batch's answer. Settle it by re-running scripts/no-events-census.py over a post-repair batch and confirming no instance is flagged DEGENERATE.
_superseded.why_this_file_still_exists: A superseded lock is evidence, not litter. The freeze script refuses to re-run over a record naming a different hash, and that refusal is the guard working. Deleting the record it guards would leave nothing to show that a lock was taken, held, and deliberately broken - which is the only reason the new one can be trusted.
